findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts fails with dynamic binding graph builds must remain bounded at 809, got 810. The CHK-003 implementer isolated the cause: it still fails with every CHK-003 source edit stashed and passes at builds=809 the moment packages/main/src/tasks/narrowing-repin-smoke.ts (created by CHK-001) is moved out of the tree, so the extra build is this story adding one scanned executable source file. Acceptance-blocking: test:retired-authority-vocabulary-guard is in the test:serial-reference chain that validate runs, so REVIEW to TEST cannot pass. Fix: raise DYNAMIC_BINDING_BUILD_CEILING from 809 to 810 with a maintenance comment stating that the ceiling counts one dynamic binding build per scanned executable source file under packages/main/src and that B-1482 CHK-001 moved it by adding the smoke; do not cite a commit hash. The same ceiling was raised 808 to 809 by story B-41c8 for the same reason.

validation-tier-planner-smoke case F-023 fails on a literal commandSetDigest pin (validation-tier-planner-smoke.ts around line 471): expected 056e47fd..., actual d98a2288.... Acceptance-blocking, because that suite is in the validate chain the REVIEW to TEST gate runs. Cause: this story CHK-003 added the narrowing-repin entry to validate.commands in proof-or-stop.config.json, which is exactly the condition the pin maintenance note names. Confirmed pre-existing to the F-001 edit by stashing that edit, rebuilding and reproducing the identical failure and digest. Fix: re-pin the literal to the value the current inventory produces, deriving it through the case own code path rather than copying it from the error message, and extend the maintenance comment to say B-1482 CHK-003 moved it by registering test:narrowing-repin. Note for the reviewer: this literal has now moved three times across three stories (B-a745, B-41c8 CHK-004, this one). Another session is replacing it with a structural assertion that the real inventory digest equals the same commands with an explicit dot cwd, which does not move when the inventory grows; that replacement is not on main yet, so this story re-pins the literal and their merge supersedes it.

review_run_start is unconditionally blocked for every REVIEW lane (concept/quality/test-coverage/docs/behavior) on this story: assertReviewerTaskContextAuthoritySafety in packages/main/src/core/prompt-envelope.ts throws severity used as sole ownership or scope authority at checklist.CHK-003.context. Root cause isolated by extracting the guard logic (lines 155-857 of prompt-envelope.ts) into a standalone harness: the single sentence "Note on priority: the story is high-risk on its merits because it edits an evidence gate; if story_creates keyword scan elevates it, keep the elevation rather than dismissing it." trips TRIAGE_SEVERITY_SUBJECT (which includes the bare word priority) co-occurring within 260 chars with TRIAGE_SEVERITY_RESPONSIBILITY_OUTCOME (which includes the bare word story) in the same clause, via hasConceptPair in classifyControlledRelationSegment for the severity-story-responsibility spec — a false positive: the sentence is about story PRIORITY elevation policy (CLAUDE.md risk-keyword elevation), not about a Finding severity determining ownership/scope. No review-runs.json exists yet for this story (confirmed by directory listing), so no reviewer lane has been able to start a run; this is not specific to the concept lane. Acceptance-blocking: REVIEW cannot proceed for any lane until this guard false-positive is resolved or CHK-003.context is reworded. Repro: see standalone extraction of prompt-envelope.ts lines 155-857 tested against the literal CHK-003.context string, which reproduces the identical error text.

docs/requirements/decisions/narrowing-only-evidence-repin.md refusal-code table (and the CHK-003/C4 smoke assertion in narrowing-repin-smoke.ts, which only checks a subset of 10 codes) both omit 3 of the 18 refusal codes the code actually emits to callers via evaluateSelectorNarrowing in core/verification.ts: narrowing_selector_unchanged (verification.ts line ~586, thrown when selector === previousSelector), narrowing_no_recorded_receipts (line ~592, thrown when no receipt has been recorded for the pinned command), and narrowing_receipt_not_predating_request (line ~679, thrown when a used receipt has no usable executedAt or claims to postdate the request). All three are real, reachable refusal paths from verification_pin_narrow (wrapped by handlers/checklist.ts narrowVerificationPin as `[${outcome.code}]` in the thrown error) but appear nowhere in the decision doc, nowhere in CLAUDE.md, and are not exercised by any of the 16 narrowing-repin-smoke.ts cases. This contradicts the storys own completeness claim: the CHK-003 commit message states the decision doc records every refusal code, and the C4 test comment says the decision doc must also carry ... every refusal code -- neither is true; both the doc and the tests list a 10-code (C4) or 15-code (doc table) subset of the real 18. Category: missing test/doc coverage, not a functional defect -- the refusals themselves work correctly.

packages/main/src/core/evidence-pin-guard.ts is untouched by this story but contains a live user-facing teaching message that is now stale residue of the pre-B-1482 absolute immutability rule. The denial verdict built at lines ~206-215 (also rendered verbatim by the generated Codex hook script in init-assets.ts renderCodexEvidencePretoolHookScript, which calls the same shared verdict logic) says: the intent is already pinned to an immutable verification (B-ec67) and your write does not match it ... Fix: run verification_run ..., or pass the exact pinned command/selector. The pin is immutable once set. This is presented as an exhaustive Fix list of exactly two options, and neither mentions verification_pin_narrow. This is precisely the scenario B-1482 was built to fix (B-a745: a pinned selector that is not discriminating), and this exact hook is what a caller/agent hits the moment they try a different selector against a bad pin -- the teaching message sends them toward re-running the same (bad) pin or matching it exactly, never toward the one legitimate escape that now exists. The categorical closing sentence The pin is immutable once set. is also no longer accurate without qualification, since B-1482 added exactly one narrowing exception. Not touched by the diff (confirmed via git diff main...HEAD, evidence-pin-guard.ts does not appear), so this is residue the story left behind rather than something it introduced.

verification_pin_narrow has no rows in PROCESS_FACT_KIND_BY_COMMAND or PROCESS_FACT_REQUIRED_SEMANTICS, so it falls back to the generic gate-evidence kind and semantics, while its siblings verification_run and verification_evidence_add carry explicit kind execution-status and semantics execution-evidence, verification-evidence, gate-evidence. The command mutates the selector every past and future receipt is judged against, so the process-fact inventory understates it. docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md names process-fact-registry.ts and PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS as the required typed-registry pair for a gate-consumed command, so only half the pair was filled. Fix: add both rows matching the siblings, and add a case asserting the new command has explicit rows rather than falling back.

Two pinned verification selectors point at cases that do not test the sentence the intent states. CHK-003:adversarial:0 describes the documentation overclaim grep but pins case C1, which tests CLI end-to-end reachability; the overclaim assertions live in C4, pinned to a different intent. CHK-002:edge:1 describes the proof asserting absence only within the retained outputTail and saying so in its message, but pins B9, the material-mismatch refusal, which never inspects message content; those assertions live in B1. Neither receipt is vacuous in the B-a745 sense, because the suite exits non-zero if any case fails, but a reader following a pinned selector to locate its claim is misled, which is the traceability the pins exist for. Because pins are immutable, the fix is to make each pinned case also assert its own intent sentence: C1 must perform the overclaim grep, and B9 must assert the outputTail-bounded wording. Also add a case asserting the decision file carries at least four pre-mortems, which CHK-003:happy:0 claims but nothing verifies.
